Break it into thirds. Start the first third truly easy, where you could hold a full conversation, settle into your normal easy pace for the middle, and only then, if you feel good, pick it up slightly for the last third. Most long runs fail because the first few miles are too fast, so holding back early is the whole trick.

If the distance feels daunting, split it mentally by landmarks or by time, like four 15-minute chunks, and take a sip of water or a quick fuel stop at each one. Run/walk intervals are also a legitimate way to build distance, and plenty of marathoners use them on purpose. For anything over about 75 minutes, take some fuel along rather than waiting until you're empty.

Are you building toward a race, or just stretching out your longest distance?
